title: Missing, expired or mis-signed JWT rejects 401 with a metadata-only audit event
asA: shelf consumer applying the edge-cloudflare-access v1.0.0 blueprint on a Workers project using the cf-edge fixture
iWant: requests carrying a missing, expired or mis-signed JWT to reject with 401 and emit exactly one metadata-only audit event on the shipped audit sink
soThat: unauthenticated traffic cannot reach the downstream handler and every reject is observable without leaking the token value

acceptanceCriteria.description: The three reject subcases (missing header, expired exp, mis-signed) each return HTTP 401 and emit exactly one audit event whose keys are drawn from {email, outcome, timestamp, path} with no token substring, no header names beyond path, and no additional keys.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a Worker fetch handler wired with createAccessValidator(...).middleware and one of the three reject subcases
acceptanceCriteria.when: the request dispatches through the validator
acceptanceCriteria.then: the validator returns 401 and emits one audit event whose outcome is drawn from {missing, expired, invalid} with the allowed-key shape

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a well-formed JWT whose aud claim does not match the elicited access-audience, when the validator checks the token, the request is refused with HTTP 401, no downstream handler runs, and exactly one metadata-only audit event with outcome:"reject" reason:"aud-mismatch" fires; the audit record carries no token substring.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the fixture applied source with the validator wired and the elicited access-audience configured
acceptanceCriteria.when: a request presents a well-formed JWT whose aud claim does not match the elicited access-audience
acceptanceCriteria.then: the validator returns 401 with reason "aud-mismatch" and emits one metadata-only audit event

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a malformed JWT (three-segment shape violated, base64url decode fails, or JSON parse fails on any segment), when the validator inspects the token, the request is refused with HTTP 401 outcome:"reject" reason:"jwt-malformed" and one metadata-only audit event fires; no downstream handler runs.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the fixture applied source with the validator wired
acceptanceCriteria.when: a request presents a malformed Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion (not three dot-separated segments, or base64url/JSON parse fails)
acceptanceCriteria.then: the validator returns 401 reason "jwt-malformed" and emits one metadata-only audit event; no downstream handler runs

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a JWT whose kid header does not resolve to any key in the current JWKS after a single forced refresh, when the validator attempts signature verification, the request is refused with HTTP 401 outcome:"reject" reason:"kid-unknown" and one metadata-only audit event fires; no downstream handler runs and no more than one JWKS refresh fires per request.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the fixture applied source with the validator wired and a JWKS whose current keys do not include the token kid
acceptanceCriteria.when: a request presents a JWT whose kid header is absent from JWKS both before and after a forced refresh
acceptanceCriteria.then: the validator returns 401 reason "kid-unknown", emits one metadata-only audit event, and no more than one JWKS refresh fires per request

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given the JWKS endpoint returns a non-2xx or a network error on both the initial fetch and the forced refresh, when the validator attempts verification, the request is refused with HTTP 503 outcome:"reject" reason:"jwks-unavailable" fail-closed and one metadata-only audit event fires; no downstream handler runs; the response carries no upstream body echo.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the fixture applied source with the validator wired and an injected fetch that fails the JWKS endpoint on both attempts
acceptanceCriteria.when: a request presents a well-formed JWT and the validator attempts to load the JWKS
acceptanceCriteria.then: the validator returns 503 reason "jwks-unavailable" (fail-closed) and emits one metadata-only audit event
